title: Join Optimization
description: Choose the right join type and order to minimize intermediate result sizes

data.text: Join optimization involves choosing the right algorithm, join order, and join type. Nested Loop, Hash Join, and Merge Join each excel under different data distributions and predicate conditions.

data.title: Common strategies
items: Nested Loop: outer row by outer row
Hash Join: hash smaller table, probe larger
Merge Join: both inputs sorted on join keys

data.title: Optimized join query
data.content: Use explicit JOIN syntax with filters to guide the optimizer.
data.code:
SELECT o.order_id, c.name, p.product_name
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE o.created_at > '2024-01-01'
  AND c.country = 'US'
ORDER BY o.created_at DESC
LIMIT 100;

data.title: Tip
data.text: Filter early with WHERE clauses to reduce intermediate result sets. The optimizer pushes down predicates but explicit filtering helps.

items.question: Does JOIN order matter?
items.answer: Modern optimizers reorder joins automatically, but statistics and hints can influence choices.

items.question: When does the optimizer choose a bad plan?
items.answer: With stale statistics, skewed data, or correlated predicates. Update statistics regularly.

items.question: Should I use subqueries instead of JOINs?
items.answer: Usually no. JOINs are more readable and often perform better. Use subqueries only when semantics require it.

data.title: Summary
points: Filter before joining to reduce row counts
Use statistics to guide index creation
Choose join types based on input size and ordering
data.takeaway: Join performance depends on data size, predicate selectivity, and index availability. Let the optimizer see accurate statistics.
